title: Affine fibre charts with vanishing differentials
statement: Let $h:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose that every scheme-theoretic fibre $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] there is an affine open covering $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_i U_i$, with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, such that the induced ring map $R\to A_i$ is finitely generated (there are finitely many elements generating $A_i$ as an $R$-algebra). For every $i$ and every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $s\in V$ correspond to $\mathfrak p$ and put $C_{i,\mathfrak p}=A_i\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the fibre ring of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with $\kappa(s)$ identified with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $$U_i\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_{i,\mathfrak p}.$$ The natural map of this fibre into $Z_s$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], with image the inverse image of $U_i$ under $Z_s\to Z$. Moreover, $\operatorname{Spec}C_{i,\mathfrak p}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is unramified and $\Omega_{C_{i,\mathfrak p}/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

proof.text: Fix $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$. By the affine-cover definition of locally finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_i U_i$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $A_i$ finitely generated over $R$. The index set need not be finite. Fix $i$ and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, corresponding to $s\in V$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ map identifies $\mathcal O_{B,s}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ as an $R$-algebra. Quotienting by their corresponding maximal ideals identifies $\kappa(s)$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to B$ defining the fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] factors through $V$, and its map to $V$ is induced by $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: both maps on $R$ send a section to its germ modulo the maximal ideal.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), stalk and germ descriptions on an affine open

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with ambient maps $Z\to B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to B$, and open subschemes $U_i$, $V$ and the whole $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. It identifies $D=U_i\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with the open inverse image of $U_i$ in $Z_s$, compatibly with both projections. Applied with ambient maps $U_i\to B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to B$, and the same base open $V$ and whole source opens, it identifies $D$ with all of $U_i\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $D$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Its second-projection formula makes this an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, not just an abstract scheme isomorphism.

The morphism $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is unramified by hypothesis. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open], its restriction to the open subscheme $D$ from step 3, with the whole target retained, is unramified. Under the base-compatible affine identification in step 3 this is the structure map of $\operatorname{Spec}C_{i,\mathfrak p}$. Apply the forward direction of [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] to $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C_{i,\mathfrak p}$: it gives $\Omega_{C_{i,\mathfrak p}/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$. Since $i$ and $\mathfrak p$ were arbitrary, all required clauses hold.

The delivery adds no new nodes, leaves the statement unchanged and has proof_deps equal to the union of the step uses. Step 1 is the affine-cover definition of locally finite type (def-weil-finite-type-morphism), with no finiteness of the cover assumed. Step 2 uses clause (c) of lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization: it gives kappa(s)=kappa(p), and Spec kappa(s)->B factors through V as Spec(R->R_p->kappa(p)); this is elementary. Step 3 applies lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product twice. In the first application f(U_i)⊆V comes from step 1 and the point map lands in V by step 2; the image is p^{-1}(U_i). The second application, with whole source opens, gives U_i x_V = U_i x_B. lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra then gives Spec(A_i ⊗_R kappa(p)) over Spec kappa(p) through its projection formulas. Step 4 restricts the unramified fibre using clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open, then applies the forward direction of the affine criterion to get Omega_{C/kappa(p)}=0. The declared tool use of lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open (unit sk-thm-p1, off the route of sk-i-curve-zero) is accepted: only its generic 02G6 open-restriction clause is used. I tested the edge cases: empty preimage, R=0, the identity, a closed immersion, and A^1, which fails the hypothesis as it should. There is no cycle: the item cites neither its parent nor its sibling.
